{"number":128,"title":"governance: the thirty-defect programme, planned against the seven-stage spine","body":"Branch restarted from `main` after #127 merged — no stacking on merged history.

Carries the programme for resolving the thirty defects registered during research batch 05 (`D05-001` … `D05-030`), planned against the seven-stage spine rather than as thirty tickets. Planned by Fable read-only, written out here, then **fact-checked and attacked by two independent read-only passes before execution**.

**`scratchpad/pr-128-defect-programme/PROGRAMME.md`** is the deliverable.

## Status: T0.1 executed, the rest of Tranche 0 held

Verification found the plan's **diagnosis sound and several of its remedies wrong**. Held rather than executed:

- **T0.3** — `DR-2026-05-09:24` defines `prior_expectation` as *"what Claude expected **before searching**"*, but `add-source` runs after the source is retrieved and read. The refusal could only be satisfied by reconstruction — the exact artefact D05-025 exists to prevent, and which the plan quotes approvingly two paragraphs earlier. The fact belongs to `log-search`.
- **T0.4** — `connections_produced` carries no per-connection direction (**6 of 15** rows are `backward=1 AND forward=1`), so the view would assert containment the data cannot support; it would turn the **blocking** `pipeline_completeness_fresh` gate red via a `user_version` bump the sweep list omits; and it would staleen CLAUDE.md's "five cross-stage views".
- **T0.2** — `.claude/settings.json` **already has a `Stop` key** running the research DoD gate, so "append a `Stop` entry" read carelessly disables it. `Stop` also fires per *turn*, and would re-copy an 11.2 MB tracked blob every turn.
- **T1.2** — factually false: it lists Wiley `pdfdirect` as "not yet tried". Both `pdfdirect` and `/epdf` are in the manifest as Cloudflare interstitials, and `REF-00975`'s own note says so.
- **T2.2** — its deletion gate greps `data_*.sql`; the 147 real INSERTs are in `057_baseline`, which that glob cannot see.

Two of the plan's own stated facts were withdrawn in-file with the reasoning kept visible: a foreign-key "correction" that compared a cross-boundary subset (7) against a total inbound count (12), and a claim of 21 retired-vocabulary hits in `transcripts/` where the audit reports 71 and names zero.

**T0.5 survived verification in full** and is ready to execute.

## What needs the owner

**A live contradiction between two ACTIVE decisions**, same ruling session, nothing superseding either:

- **D-0173** — *"The concept vocabulary is harvested at evidence and adjudicated at judgment. DR-2026-08-24 §2.4 deferral to synthesis is OVERRULED."*
- **D-0174** — *"Relevance is an adjudication made at evidence collection; **applicability remains a synthesis judgement**."*

D-0173's ACTION orders two new tables (`observed_terms`, `term_adjudications`) that the programme's §6 forbids, and still owes a `CLAUDE.md` §6 correction — that file continues to teach *"zero `item_population_links` is the correct pre-synthesis state"* verbatim.

`§7a` (`.ignore` scope for `transcripts/`) was **decided and landed** — the JSONL is hidden from ripgrep, README and every `index.json` stay searchable. The first pattern failed a planted-token test and was replaced.

## Also in this PR

Rule 6 in `CLAUDE.md` stuttered *"Owner directive 2026-08-25"* twice; the scratchpad convention endorsed guessing a PR number; two commit timestamps were typed rather than derived; a planner transcript was filed as `other`; and the command-log hook recorded the very commit that committed it, making the stop hook and the log hook mutually recursive with no exit.

# DR-2026-08-19 — The operative instrument: restart research, end the loop

> **THIS DOCUMENT SUPERSEDES ALL OTHER PLANNING DOCUMENTS IN THIS REPOSITORY.**
> It is the only planning artifact a session needs to read, and it is meant to be **run**, not
> consulted. On ratification, every document in the supersession table below becomes historical
> record: readable for provenance, binding on nothing.

## §A How to use this document

| If you are | Read |
|---|---|
| The owner, ratifying | §9 (twelve decisions, one sitting), then sign §2.5 |
| A session about to work | §A → §3 (order) → §12 (the runbook) → run it |
| A session tempted to write a plan | §11. The check will reject your commit |
| Anyone checking what binds | §B below |

Two documents remain live alongside this one, and neither is a plan:

- **`CLAUDE.md`** — the repo's mechanical map (write path, gates, traps). Auto-loaded; a reference,
  not an instruction set. Where it disagrees with this instrument, this instrument wins and CLAUDE.md
  is the thing to correct.
- **`references/project-standards.md`** — the append-only operative rule ledger. Rules land there by
  design and machinery reads it. This instrument cites it; it does not restate it.

Everything else is superseded.

## §B Supersession table

| Document | Status on ratification |
|---|---|
| `workplan/next-steps-synthesis-2026-07-14.md` | **DISCHARGED** — freeze unsatisfiable (§2.5); §5 identity question answered by DR-2026-07-21 |
| `workplan/phase-e-execution-log-2026-07-14.md` | **SPENT** — pilot substrate destroyed by DR-2026-08-06; the "external review DECLINED" ruling carries forward per §10.2 |
| `workplan/2026-08-11-reconciled-findings-register.md` | **HISTORICAL** — R-01, R-06/07/08 verified resolved; **R-12 and R-17b transferred forward** (§10.7) |
| `workplan/2026-08-16-adversarial-critique-and-execution-plan.md` | **SUPERSEDED** — findings stand, sequencing dead |
| `workplan/2026-08-17-consolidated-action-plan.md` | **SUPERSEDED** — throughlines T1–T5 retained as diagnosis; only I-08 ever landed; §5's migration-number allocation table survives as the sole allocator |
| `workplan/2026-08-18-structural-census-and-cull-list.md` | **EVIDENCE, not instruction** — governs the cull where it and the cull plan differ |
| `workplan/2026-08-18-cull-execution-plan.md` (incl. §14, §15) | **DEFERRED behind the batch** — §15 is the route; §0.3 governs its value ("adds zero rows") |
| `workplan/2026-08-18-research-frame-proposal.md` | **RULING RECORD** — R1–R6 preserved; R1's strip *mechanism* overturned by §1 |
| `workplan/2026-08-18-handoff-next-session.md` | **HISTORICAL** — §2 rulings and §7 traps absorbed here; **§6 sequence overturned** by §3 |

## §3 What this unblocks, and in what order

The restart plan §7 already establishes that no cull phase is a prerequisite. This decision
extends that: **no schema phase is a prerequisite either.** Every input the first batch reads is
live today — `slugs` 106, `term_aliases` 2,382, `axes`/`access_needs` and their 232 mapping rows,
`jurisdictional_values` 109. Every table it writes exists and is empty.

1. ~~Owner adopts or rejects this DR.~~ **DONE 2026-08-19 — RATIFIED (OD-1).**
2. ~~Fix the write path, the read path and the two transaction defects — F3–F6.~~ **DONE
   2026-08-19.** `db.py connect()` no longer sets `journal_mode`, and 16 pure-read call sites
   pass `readonly=True` (F4); `migrate_db.py` applies body, FK verdict and ledger row in one
   transaction with the pragmas hoisted (F5/F6); `emit_data_migration.py` no longer wraps bodies;
   `scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py` is the capture path (F3). Proved by
   `migrate_db.py --selftest` (14 cases) and `emit_batch_sql.py --selftest` (9 cases), and by a
   rebuild that reproduces every table count identically.
3. ~~Seed the three missing DoD selftest cases (R9, R12, R15).~~ **DONE 2026-08-19** —
   `research_batch_dod.py --selftest` now asserts all fifteen rules and prints 15/15.
4. ~~**Run the first research batch** — restart plan §§2–3, unchanged, under the §1.4 quarantine.~~
   **DONE 2026-08-19** — `session_2026-08-19-research-batch-01-room-acoustic-performance`:
   9 `search_executions`, 5 `evidence_sources`, 5 `source_slug_links`, 12 `evidence_population_match`.
   Its five admissions were first written with **fabricated author lists**, corrected the same day
   against persisted Crossref payloads; `GAP-B01-001` holds the content re-read open.
4a. **The owner decision batch OD-A … OD-G** —
   `workplan/2026-08-22-agonist-antagonist-execution-plan.md` §2. **← THIS IS THE NEXT ACT, and it
   is the owner's, not a session's.** OD-A (are `item_population_links` substrate or scaffolding —
   all 372 carry `rationale_ref` NULL), OD-B (do deaf and hard-of-hearing people belong on
   `room-acoustic-performance`), OD-C (A-18's applicability set), OD-D/OD-E (two tier re-grades),
   OD-F (the adversarial-subject waiver), OD-G (strike step 10's `jurisdictional_values` clause).
   **Nothing in step 5 can be authored until OD-A, OD-B and OD-C are answered.**
5. Render **a** determination and read it — for a cell chosen **applicability-edge-first**, not
   the cell this DR's original framing implied. **AMENDED 2026-08-22.** As written, step 5 pointed
   at A-18 × AUT; `BRK-20` established that A-18 carries **zero** `item_population_links` and its
   only route to a population is the axis map, which owner directive D-1 quarantines. Authoring
   that cell today would render a coverage failure as an epistemic finding — the
   `workplan/2026-08-20-adversarial-adjudication-a18-aut.md` refusal, which stands.
6. Only then: re-key or retire `jurisdictional_values`; re-scope handoff step 8 with its full
   dependency cascade; re-arm the retired `min_items` guards.

   ten-day window and none was built; fourteen of the fifteen citations were written inside those ten
   days. **This step now owns all four. Each is ONE open item and is named once, here:**

   | # | Item | Locations that specified it | State |
   |---|---|---|---|

   | 6b | `db.py` write helpers (`add-authors`, `next-ref-id`, `add-match`, `finish-search`) | writer plan Phase 2 · walk plan Phase 7 · §12.5 of this DR | Not built; batch 2 ran and did not automate them. Hand SQL is the write path. |
   | 6c | `GB` → `UK` in `jurisdictional_values` (20 rows) | handoff §6.4 · 08-19 critique §7.7 · frame proposal §10.4 · 08-14 I-20 | **Correct and blocked, not wrong** — `jurisdiction-philosophy.md` §3.3 mandates `UK` at ERROR level and the project overrode ISO deliberately. Blocked by the REFERENCE-ONLY quarantine; clears with **OD-G**. **And its enforcer never opens the DB** (`validate_jurisdiction.py` parses YAML only), which is why it survived four schedulings. Wire the enforcer in the same change that fixes the rows, never before. |
   | 6d | OD-5 — R9 blind to `source_locators` | digestion · A-18 adjudication §8.6 · walk plan · 08-22 F-18 | **DONE 2026-08-23** — `R9a`/`R9b`. The naive widening was refuted first: all four DOIs held in both tables carry the *same* ref_id, so failing on overlap would have failed correct promotions. |

Step 4 populated `evidence_sources` and `source_slug_links` — two of the six invariant tables the
blocking reproducibility gate compares. **Running the batch first is what made the later schema
work safe to run at all.**

> **AMENDMENT 2026-08-22 — why this section was edited rather than superseded.** Step 4 read
> *"← THIS IS THE NEXT ACT"* for three days after it was completed, so an agent obeying CLAUDE.md
> lines 9–12 (*"the instrument wins"*) was directed at step 5, and step 5 pointed at the one cell
> the project had already refused on evidence. The halt was recorded only in
> `sessions/session_2026-08-20-provenance-walk.md` §7, which does not bind. That is a defect in
> this instrument, not in the session record, and §5's reversal clause makes correcting it here
> the cheaper repair. **No successor DR is written, and none is owed.**

---

## §4 Acceptance — the one criterion apparatus cannot satisfy

Every criterion currently in play can be met by building apparatus: a gate exits 0, a rebuild
reproduces, a test scores 72/72, a metric moves. That is why apparatus is always the locally valid
move, and it is the whole of the loop.

**Proposed single criterion, replacing restart-plan §4 criterion 6** (which F7 of the adversarial
critique shows is made unreachable by handoff step 8):

> **One answered question, published.** One research question, with a determination, its governing
> sources, its population-match grading, and its search log *including the empty searches* —
> rendered and readable as output, not as a row count and not as a green check.

No script, registry entry, check, decision record, or plan can satisfy that. Only research can.

---

## §5 Reversal

Both decisions are reversible by a later DR recorded here. The freeze expires by its own terms the
moment `evidence_sources` is non-empty; it needs no repeal. Decision 1 is a handling rule for a
table that is archived rather than deleted under R1, so nothing it governs is destroyed.

**This DR proposes no successor document, and none is owed.** The next artifact should be a search
log.

---

The sections below were added after the audit that this DR's §2 anticipated. They convert it from
two decisions into **the single binding instrument** the adjudication ruled for. Sections 0–5 above
stand unchanged.

## §2.5 Freeze supersession — the clause the owner signs

A governance freeze already exists. `workplan/next-steps-synthesis-2026-07-14.md` §2.6 declared it;

```

```

## 1. Four mechanisms, not thirty defects

The register looks like thirty independent bugs. It is four, and the fourth was not in the
original hypothesis.

**(a) A writer that cannot express a state its own checker accepts.** `insert_source` wrote
`VERIFIED` with disposition `OPEN`, which invariant I1 forbids outright; `log_mining` never set
the status C08's biconditional asserts; the `match_id` derivation made the doctrinal adversarial
dissent unwritable. All fixed. **Still live in half-fixed form: D05-025.** `add-source` gained
`--prior-expectation`, but `insert_source` still refuses `VERIFIED` without
`verification_method` and *not* without a prior — so it can still write rows CHECK 7 rejects.

**The mirror also exists, and is worth naming: a checker with no writer.**
`metadata_integrity_status` has no writer that ever leaves `CORRECTED`, and
`judgment/convergence-independence` has no convergence writer at all. A gate whose satisfying
writer does not exist is a trap; that is why T2.1 waits.

**(b1) A gate examining a proxy where the property IS decidable from data already held.** D05-023.
The remedy is a pointer, then a gate that reads it.

**(b2) A gate examining a proxy where the property is NOT machine-decidable.** D05-021 (harm
findings live in a brief the database never sees), D05-022 (a rationale weighed against a
payload). **The remedy here is emphatically not a new check** — it would be vacuous or red by
construction. The remedy is that the gate stops printing more than it asserted, and the property
is routed to the adversarial pass as a standing subject.

**(c) Provenance depending on memory.** D05-029, D05-018, D05-025. The unifying rule, which the
already-fixed members of this class all obey: *the artefact is written by the tool at capture
time, never reconstructed afterwards.* That is why `prior_expectation` is not backfilled with a
prior, and why D05-029 needs a hook rather than a habit.

**(d) Substrate presuppositions — not in the original hypothesis.** D05-001 and D05-002 are a
column and a table that would hold a **synthesis output** upstream of synthesis. Their correct fix
is the *absence* of work until synthesis exists, plus a doctrine text that currently contradicts
the ruling (§7(c), first item — corrected 2026-09-03 from "§7b", which is the `serves_icf`
rename deferral and has nothing to do with the contradiction).

**The holistic link.** (b2) is gated by the adversarial pass, and the adversarial pass is gated by
leaving its workings on disk. **Fixing D05-029 is what makes D05-021 and D05-022 "gated" at all.**
That is the programme's spine, and it is why a transcript hook sits in the same plan as a
convergence view.

naming batch-02 while batch-03 was the newest session with research rows.

Full narrative in `scratchpad/pr-127-research-batch-05-circulation-icf/`:
`FRAME.md`, `agonist/BRIEF.md`, `antagonist/FINDINGS.md`, `tracer/LOG.md`, and
`DEFECT-REGISTER.md`, which is the single home of defect status.

`antagonist/FINDINGS.md` was written up after the fact by the orchestrator rather than by
the agent, which ran read-only and wrote nothing. That directory stood empty beside the
agonist's and the tracer's files until the omission was noticed — the pass that produced
the session's most valuable findings had no review surface, which is the exact failure
rule 6 names. It records what the agent claimed, what re-verification sustained, the one
place it over-counted, and the one place the orchestrator disagreed and why.
=== FINDINGS ===
## The findings that were worth the batch

**Circulation geometry is the most-cited in-building barrier disabled people report.**
Euan's Guide Access Survey 2025 (REF-00978, Co-1, over 4,400 respondents, 88% of them
disabled people), question 7, p.13–14: *"I could not get around the venue (e.g. lack of
lifts, narrow corridors, too little space or poor layout)"* — **56%**, against *"could
not get into the venue"* 41% and *"no access to a toilet that suits my requirements"*
41%. Second of twelve options overall, behind parking at 64%.

**The shoulder-load penalty is incurred by the existence of a slope, not by its
steepness.** Marchiori, Gagnon & Pradon 2023 (REF-00973), Table 3: shoulder
flexion/extension push-phase HIGH risk runs 12.2% level → 44.5% → 47.0% → 45.2% across
1:20, 1:16, 1:12. The authors' own reading: *"greater efforts are required to propulse
the wheelchair from the smallest slope (2.7°), but that this effort does not increase
further with the increasing slope."* A frame built from an item called "Ramp Gradient
(≤1:20)" would have gone looking for the difference between 1:20 and 1:12 and found the
wrong question.

**A published error, flagged.** That same paper's §2.2 says *"The four slopes greater
than 0° corresponded to slopes that increase from one unit of height to 20, 16, 12 and 8
units of length"* — four ratios for three slopes. arctan settles the mapping:
2.86°/3.58°/4.76° ⇒ 1:20/1:16/1:12. **1:8 is 7.13° and was never tested.** Anyone citing
this paper for a 1:8 result cites its error.

**Ramp *descent* outranks fast propulsion for shoulder load**, and the discourse is all
about ascent (REF-00974, abstract-level locator, ten able-bodied participants — the
ordering is the claim, not the newtons).

**A 49-record Japanese J-STAGE seam invisible to English engines**, including 2003 prior
art (REF-00976, admitted under R5: non-English peer-reviewed work is academic, and
non-indexation is an indexing fact).

  {migrate,gaps,connections,is-mined,log-mining,add-candidate,add-population-match,add-jurisdictional-value,add-economics-entry,add-case-study,add-code-lead,correct-source,amend-search,resolve-candidate,amend-source,update-locator,add-locator,next-id,coverage,synonyms,add-gap,close-gap,add-connection,update-connection,unmined,upsert-coverage,upsert-language,log-search,update-bpc,add-source,add-conflict,update-conflict,conflicts,delete-connection,add-item,items,add-audit-run,update-audit-run,audit-runs,add-supersession-check,add-gap-mining,update-gap-addressability,unmined-gaps}
    migrate             Run pending schema migrations
    gaps                Query gaps
    connections         Query connections
    is-mined            Check mining status
    log-mining          Log citation mining
    add-candidate       Stage a screened candidate (search_candidates)
    add-population-match
                        Grade population-of-study vs population-served (R13)
    add-jurisdictional-value
                        Record a code/regulatory value (T4-T6 stratum)
    add-economics-entry
                        Record a Part-13 economics finding
    add-case-study      Record a Part-12 case study
    add-code-lead       Record a code/standard lead (research_code_leads)
    correct-source      Rewrite bibliographic fields FROM THE LOGGED PAYLOAD
    amend-search        APPEND a dated correction to a logged search's
                        findings_note
    resolve-candidate   Close a staged candidate, re-describing it from the
                        source (R15)
    amend-source        Correct a JUDGEMENT field on an evidence row,
                        recording what was replaced
    update-locator      Move a lead's status in the clue store
    add-locator         Write a lead into the clue store
    next-id             Get next available ID
    coverage            Check search coverage
    synonyms            Get synonyms for item
    add-gap             Insert a new gap record
    close-gap           Close a gap record
    add-connection      Insert a new connection record
    update-connection   Update connection status
    unmined             List unmined Tier 1-N sources
    upsert-coverage     Update search coverage for slug+jurisdiction
    upsert-language     Update search language for slug
    log-search          Append one row to search_executions (replaces upsert-
                        coverage/-language)
    update-bpc          Update bpc_metadata for a slug
    add-source          Insert an evidence source
    add-conflict        Insert a conflict record
    update-conflict     Update a conflict record
    conflicts           Query conflict records
    delete-connection   Hard-delete a connection by CON-ID (data corrections
                        only)
    add-item            Insert an item record
    items               Query items
    add-audit-run       Create an item_audit_runs record
    update-audit-run    Update an item_audit_runs record
    audit-runs          Query item_audit_runs
    add-supersession-check
                        Record a per-anchor-source supersession outcome
                        (DR-2026-05-24)
    add-gap-mining      Record a gap-driven mining attempt (DR-2026-05-26)
    update-gap-addressability

# scratchpad/ — one folder per PR, named for it

**Owner directive 2026-09-02: name the folder for the PR concerned.**

    scratchpad/pr-<number>-<short-slug>/
    scratchpad/CURRENT            <- names the folder the command-log hook writes to

`pr-127-research-batch-05-circulation-icf/` is the shape. The PR number comes first so
the folder sorts and greps by the thing a reviewer actually has in hand.

## `CURRENT` is not decoration — it is what makes the command log land in the right place

`.claude/hooks/record-command.py` appends one JSON line per Bash call to
`<the current folder>/commands.jsonl`. **It reads `scratchpad/CURRENT` first**, and only
falls back to inference if that file is missing or names no real directory.

**So a new batch sets `CURRENT` when it creates its folder, before running anything.**

```sh
mkdir -p scratchpad/pr-128-<slug>
printf 'pr-128-<slug>' > scratchpad/CURRENT
```

Forget it, and the hook infers — which is how, on 2026-09-02, **all 969 lines of three
project sessions ended up in one directory** while the newest batch had no command log at
all. The hook's own docstring called the harness session id "the anchor"; it is not. That
id identifies the *harness* session, and one harness session spans as many project
sessions as the container survives. So the hook matched the first directory it ever wrote
to and returned it forever, locking onto its own first mistake — which is why the
misfiling was total rather than partial (D05-004).

`CURRENT` moves at **open**. That is the whole point, and it is the opposite of
`sessions/LATEST` and `sessions/LATEST-RESEARCH`, which CLAUDE.md §7 warns both move at
**close** and therefore name the PREVIOUS session for the entire life of the current one.

## The folder name is not the session id

They are different things and only one of them is renameable.

The **session id** — `session_2026-09-02-research-batch-05-circulation-icf` — is written

input.command: sed -n '40,90p' scratchpad/README.md

content.content:
The **session id** — `session_2026-09-02-research-batch-05-circulation-icf` — is written
into committed data migrations, into `created_by_session` on every row it wrote, into
`sessions/LATEST`, and into the gate scopes. It is immutable in practice. The **folder** is
just where the working files live, and it is named for the PR.

One PR can hold more than one session. `pr-126-...` holds batch 04 *and* the repairs
session that followed it, because both landed in PR #126.

## Older folders keep their `session_*` names, deliberately

Fourteen directories predate this convention. Their PRs are merged, their references are
settled, and renaming them would be churn against frozen records for no reader's benefit.
The hook matches **both** prefixes. Do not "finish the job" by renaming them.

## Frozen records inside these folders were NOT rewritten by the rename

Agent briefs, tracer logs, audit logs and provenance logs still say
`scratchpad/session_2026-09-0X-.../`, because that is where those files were when those
agents wrote about them. They are records of what was true on their date. If you are
following a path out of one of those and it does not exist, this rename is why — the
`session_` stem maps to the `pr-` folder holding the same slug.

## What belongs here

Working files that are a review surface: frames, agent briefs and findings, defect
registers, audit logs, command logs. **Commit them at every natural break, not at session
end** (CLAUDE.md rule 6) — a scratchpad that lives only in context is not a review surface,
and compaction, session end and container reclamation all take it.

Agent *transcripts* are not here: they go to `transcripts/` via
`scripts/preserve_transcripts.py`. See `transcripts/README.md`.

input.body:
Branch restarted from `main` after #127 merged — no stacking on merged history.

Carries the programme for resolving the defects registered during research batch 05, planned against the seven-stage spine rather than as a list of tickets. Planned by a read-only planner pass, written out separately, then **fact-checked and attacked by three independent read-only passes** — two before execution, one adversarial steelman afterwards, which is the pass that caught what the first two and the writer all missed.

**`scratchpad/pr-128-defect-programme/PROGRAMME.md`** is the deliverable. **`scratchpad/pr-127-research-batch-05-circulation-icf/DEFECT-REGISTER.md`** is the single home of defect status.

---

## Status: Tranche 0 complete. Nothing waits on the owner. Blocked only on a merge conflict.

**Body brought current 2026-09-09.** It described the state at the third commit of twenty-six and had gone stale in the direction that matters most — it asked the owner to resolve a contradiction that verification has since withdrawn.

### ⚠️ Blocked: merge conflict on `data/guidebook.db`

`main` advanced to `938fde9` on 2026-09-07 — the scheduled `source-verification` workflow committing the DB blob. `git merge-tree` conflicts on that binary file.

The conflict is trivial in substance and structural in cause:

- **Substance.** Diffed against this PR's base `2a1ef12`, the main-side change is **exactly one `pipeline_runs` row** — run `2026-09-07 10:57`, every phase counter `0`, `doi_before/after` 8, `verified_before/after` 9. Pure telemetry, no evidence or governance content.
- **Cause.** That row was written **straight into the committed DB, not through a migration**, which is what `CLAUDE.md` rule 3 forbids in as many words. `migrate_db.py --rebuild` cannot reproduce it. And because the workflow is scheduled, it will conflict with **every** open PR that touches the DB, on a cadence nobody chose.

The resolution is to take this branch's DB (`user_version` 70, reproducible from migrations) and let the next scheduled run re-emit its telemetry. The workflow's write path is a separate defect worth its own change.

### Verification found the diagnosis sound and several remedies wrong

Held, replaced or superseded rather than executed — full reasoning in `PROGRAMME.md` §3a:

- **T0.2** — `.claude/settings.json` **already has a `Stop` key** running the research DoD gate, so "append a `Stop` entry" read carelessly disables it. `Stop` also fires per *turn* and would re-copy an 11.2 MB tracked blob every turn. **Superseded:** the log/commit recursion was fixed at its cause, and a **`SubagentStop`** hook now runs `preserve_transcripts.py` at the one moment a subagent's workings are complete and at maximum risk (D05-039).
- **T0.3** — `DR-2026-05-09:24` defines `prior_expectation` as *"what Claude expected **before searching**"*, but `add-source` runs after the source is retrieved and read, so any value it took could only be reconstruction — the exact artefact D05-025 exists to prevent. **Replaced:** migrations 069/070 move the field to `search_executions`, `log-search` now **refuses** without it, `add-source` lost the flag, and CHECK 7 is repointed through `v_source_admission`.
- **T0.4** — `connections_produced` carries no per-connection direction (**6 of 15** rows are `backward=1 AND forward=1`), so the view would assert containment the data cannot support. **Declined**; the containment query became a standing subject of the adversarial pass instead.
- **T1.2** — factually false: it lists Wiley `pdfdirect` as "not yet tried". Both `pdfdirect` and `/epdf` are in the manifest as Cloudflare interstitials, and `REF-00975`'s own note says so.
- **T2.2** — its deletion gate greps `data_*.sql`; the 147 real INSERTs are in `057_baseline`, which that glob cannot see.
- **§6** — *"no new tables and no new columns"* was a scope rule written as a standing prohibition, against **D-0173**, an ACTIVE owner ruling that had already ordered the harvest. `CLAUDE.md` rule 0: a live directive is not answerable to paperwork, and a scope rule is paperwork. **Superseded**; the harvest landed in migration 068.

### ~~What needs the owner~~ — WITHDRAWN 2026-09-03

**The reported D-0173 / D-0174 contradiction is not a contradiction.** D-0173 rules on the concept *vocabulary*; D-0174 rules that *relevance* is adjudicated at collection while *applicability* stays a synthesis judgement. Those are different objects. The apparent clash sat in D-0173's agent-written sweep note, not in either ruling. **`CLAUDE.md` §6 needs no correction and no decision is owed.**

**`§7a` (`.ignore` scope for `transcripts/`) was decided and landed.** The JSONL is hidden from ripgrep; README and every `index.json` stay searchable. The first pattern failed a planted-token test and was replaced — `**` excludes the session directory and gitignore cannot re-include a file whose parent is excluded, so the entry matches by extension instead.

### Nine defects found after this body was first written

`D05-031` … `D05-039`, all resolved, three of them P1. They were found by trying to use the things this PR built, and by an adversarial audit — not by the suite:

- **D05-031** — `dbcore.WRITABLE_TABLES` listed 14 tables and neither of migration 068's, so the sanctioned capture path could not carry a single row of the harvest it had just shipped a writer for. **Third time** that one list has been blind to a live table.
- **D05-033** — the harvest had a rule, a writer and **no reader**. A batch admitting nine sources and harvesting zero was fully compliant with every gate. `research_batch_dod.py` now carries `R11-harvest`, scoped to admissions, proven to fail.
- **D05-034** — the command-log hook was a **SyntaxError for two hours** and its own test passed green over it, because `load()` execs only the text above the `try:`. Migrations 068/069/070, the `db.py` work and the whole harvest have no command log at all.
- **D05-035** — the `ref_id` sweep stopped 24 lines short *inside a file it swept*, leaving two skills and a gate's own failure advice teaching a rule that mints a live evidence row. **A skill is a caller.**
- **D05-036** — a §2(b) correction that was itself the §2(b) defect: it measured the post-exemption tree and reported it as the pre-exemption one.
- **D05-037** — "corrected" written into the execution record while the text was never touched. The session's recurring pattern, occurring inside the section built to stop it.

### Still open, deliberately

`D05-021`, `D05-022`, `D05-023` stay **OPEN as gate defects**. Each is a property that is not machine-decidable, or whose gate would be a trap without a writer. The remedy is a durable human subject, not a check: `skills/adversarial-research_SKILL.md` now carries **"Standing subjects of every adversarial pass"** naming all three, with the containment SQL to run in place of the view T0.4 correctly declined to build. `D05-018` is open for Goodwin only; `D05-024` is closed as accepted.

## What this changes for batch 06

Research is **not** blocked, and Tranche 1 runs beside it. Three things change for an agent:

1. `log-search` requires `--prior-expectation` and refuses an empty string.
2. Every admitted source must carry at least one `observe-term` observation, or `R11-harvest` fails.
3. Subagent transcripts land on disk by hook; the session still commits them under rule 6.

Schema moves `user_version` 67 → 70. `observed_terms` holds 33 rows; `term_adjudications` is empty by design until judgment exists.

## Also in this PR

`CLAUDE.md` rule 6 stuttered *"Owner directive 2026-08-25"* twice; the scratchpad convention endorsed guessing a PR number; two commit timestamps were typed rather than derived; a planner transcript was filed as `other`; and the command-log hook recorded the very commit that committed it, making the stop hook and the log hook mutually recursive with no exit.

## Short answer

**Yes, you can start research — after merging PR #128, not before.** Nothing else blocks a batch. But research is not what the project is short of, and that is the thing worth knowing before you spend a day on it.

---

## Where the project actually is

Measured against `origin/main` at `938fde9`, `user_version` 67, today.

| Stage | State |
|---|---|
| **base** | Healthy. 106 slugs (80 active, 23 stub), 2,382 term aliases, 88 terms, 23 populations, 17 access needs, 17 ICF axes, 881 identifier leads, 83 code leads |
| **research** | 43 logged searches on **two** slugs — `room-acoustic-performance` (28), `accessible-circulation-geometry` (15) |
| **evidence** | **9 admitted sources.** All from batch 05, all on `accessible-circulation-geometry`, all verified against retrieved payloads. 14 population-match rows (2 exact, 7 partial, 5 proxy) |
| **judgment** | **0 rows** |
| **synthesis** | **0 rows** |
| **specification** | **0 rows** |
| **render** | 0 cells determined, 0 slugs synthesized |

Gates are green: a full local run is **47 passing, zero blocking failures**, 9 advisory. PR #128's CI is 12/12.

So the apparatus is in good order and the book is empty. That is not new, but two things about it are.

**Your 2026-09-01 ruling was executed completely.** The item layer is gone — 93 items, 540 taxonomy links, 147 term links, 109 jurisdictional values, and batches 01–03's evidence retracted with them. The search logs were kept. The 9 sources you have are the entire live evidence base, and they are the only ones that were ever built under the corrected writers.

**The findings from batch 05 are good.** Circulation geometry is the most-cited *in-building* barrier disabled people report (56%, second of twelve behind parking). The shoulder-load penalty is incurred by a slope existing, not by its steepness — 12.2% risk at level, then 44.5 / 47.0 / 45.2% across 1:20, 1:16, 1:12. An item named "Ramp Gradient (≤1:20)" would have sent you looking for the difference between 1:20 and 1:12 and you would have found the wrong question. That is your own thesis about contaminated item names, confirmed by evidence.

---

## The one thing that is actually broken

`specifications.item_code` is `NOT NULL REFERENCES items(item_code)`, and `items` holds zero rows. I proved it on a scratch copy:

```
items rows: 0
INSERT REFUSED: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed
```

**A determination currently has nowhere to land.** Deleting the item layer was right, and it severed the table the determination writes into. Judgment and synthesis are fine — both key on `slug`, which is alive.

Compounding it: `db.py` has 42 subcommands and **not one writes judgment, synthesis or specification**. The back half of your pipeline has no sanctioned write path at all. That is why `§4` of the operative instrument — *one answered question, published* — has not moved in three weeks. It is not blocked on research. It is blocked on there being no way to write down what the research means.

---

## What remains, in order

1. **Merge PR #128.** Blocked by a merge conflict (below).
2. **Decide what a determination is keyed on now.** `(item × population)` is dead. Slug × population? Slug × parameter × population? This is a `DG-NON` content decision and it is yours — it is the only thing I found that genuinely needs you.
3. **Build the judgment writer**, then synthesis, then specification. Three `db.py` subcommands, in that order, each landing with its gate.
4. Then batch 06 — or batch 06 first, in parallel, since it is independent of 2 and 3.
5. Housekeeping: five open `GAP` rows all describe retracted evidence and should be closed or restated.

If you want one day's work to feel like progress, **do 2 and 3 before more research.** You have enough evidence on one slug to produce your first determination; you have no way to record it.

---

## PR #128 — updated

The body described the state at commit 3 of 26. I rewrote it and left one comment.

**The important correction: it was asking you to resolve a D-0173 / D-0174 contradiction that does not exist.** D-0173 rules on the concept vocabulary; D-0174 on relevance versus applicability. Different objects. The clash was in an agent-written sweep note, not in either ruling. That request sat there for six days. **Nothing in the PR waits on you.**

**It is blocked by a merge conflict on `data/guidebook.db`,** and the cause matters more than the fix. `main` moved on 2026-09-07 when the scheduled `source-verification` workflow ran. Because it is scheduled, it will do this to every open PR that touches the DB indefinitely.

Resolving it is taking the branch's DB and letting the next run re-emit its telemetry. **Say the word and I'll do it and get #128 merged.** The workflow's write path deserves a separate fix.

I also opened **PR #129** for one piece of hygiene this session created: the command-log hook was appending my calls to PR #127's committed log, because `scratchpad/CURRENT` still pointed there. Moved and repointed.

I deliberately did not write a status document. `DR-2026-08-19` §11 makes that the exact artefact class that produced the recursion you are trying to escape.

## What happened

`scratchpad/CURRENT` still named `pr-127-research-batch-05-circulation-icf`, so `.claude/hooks/record-command.py` appended 23 lines of this session's Bash calls to that PR's committed command log — **D05-004's failure class, in the directory whose README documents it.** The hook is behaving correctly; `CURRENT` moves at open and this session never moved it.

- The 23 lines move to `scratchpad/project-status-overview-8fpu75/commands.jsonl`.
- `pr-127-research-batch-05-circulation-icf/commands.jsonl` is restored byte-identical to `HEAD`.
- `scratchpad/CURRENT` repointed.

The folder is named for the **branch**, not a guessed PR number. `scratchpad/README.md` as amended on PR #128 rules that guessing a number and landing on it "is worse than being wrong — a guess that lands teaches nobody", and prescribes `git mv` once the number is known. That rename follows in this PR.

## What this PR deliberately does not add

No status document. `DR-2026-08-19` §11 property 5 makes the test explicit: a session that commits anything other than the §3 fixes, a record-correction, search logs, migrations or a rendered determination has failed the instrument's own termination property. A repository-state summary is exactly the artefact class that produced the recursion. The findings of the pass were delivered to the owner in conversation, and the durable ones are recorded where they belong — on PR #128.

# and a handler that turned sqlite3.OperationalError into a silent `skip (no such
# table)`. Measured 2026-08-28 against the pending seven-stage rename: ALL SIX

#
# The skip existed for a real case ("a table may legitimately not exist in an
# older schema version"), but it cannot tell that case from "renamed and nobody
# swept me", which is the case this gate is FOR. Under a version mismatch,
# schema_version already reports it, so nothing is lost by making absence loud.
#
# Comparing every table costs nothing measurable (~66 COUNT(*) over a 3.6 MB DB)
# and is strictly stronger: measured the same day, a fresh rebuild reproduces the
# committed database on every table, so this cries no wolf.
SCHEMA_VERSION_INVARIANT = ("PRAGMA user_version", "schema_version")

EXEMPT_TABLES = ("evidence_source_authors", "pipeline_runs")

# Columns whose divergence is bookkeeping rather than substance. Kept separate so
# --deep can say "277 rows differ, all of them only in updated_at" instead of
# reporting that as content drift and being ignored for crying wolf.
VOLATILE_COLUMNS = frozenset({
    "created_at", "updated_at", "last_updated",
    "created_by_session", "updated_by_session",
})

# data_migrations is the ledger *of* the rebuild, so comparing its application
# provenance compares the run to itself: applied_at is when this run applied each
# migration, and the runner stamps notes='rebuilt by runner'. What must match is
# which migrations exist and what their content hashed to. Handled by name rather
# than by adding "notes"/"applied_at" to VOLATILE_COLUMNS, which would blind the
# comparison to genuine drift in any other table carrying a column so named.
LEDGER_TABLE = "data_migrations"
LEDGER_COLUMNS = ("migration_id", "content_sha")


def db_path():
    return os.environ.get("GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH", os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "data", "guidebook.db"))

{"number":129,"title":"governance: this session's command log was landing in PR #127's folder","body":"Opened for a read-only status pass over the repository. The only content change is repository hygiene the pass itself created.

## What happened

`scratchpad/CURRENT` still named `pr-127-research-batch-05-circulation-icf`, so `.claude/hooks/record-command.py` appended 23 lines of this session's Bash calls to that PR's committed command log — **D05-004's failure class, in the directory whose README documents it.** The hook is behaving correctly; `CURRENT` moves at open and this session never moved it.

## What this changes

- The 23 lines move to `scratchpad/project-status-overview-8fpu75/commands.jsonl`.
- `pr-127-research-batch-05-circulation-icf/commands.jsonl` is restored byte-identical to `HEAD`.
- `scratchpad/CURRENT` repointed.

The folder is named for the **branch**, not a guessed PR number. `scratchpad/README.md` as amended on PR #128 rules that guessing a number and landing on it "is worse than being wrong — a guess that lands teaches nobody", and prescribes `git mv` once the number is known. content.text:
The stop hook caught a real defect, not just an untracked file.

**What it was.** `preserve_transcripts.py` wrote `index.json` only `if index` — and `index` holds *subagent* rows only, since the loop skips `main.jsonl` by name. So a session that ran no subagents preserved its transcript into a directory containing exactly one file, `main.jsonl`, which `.ignore` hides. Measured before the fix, by the same planted-token method #128 used on the `.ignore` pattern itself:

```
rg --files transcripts/
  transcripts/harness_6a6f63cd/index.json      <- had subagents
  transcripts/README.md
                                               <- harness_292c6e38 absent entirely
```

`transcripts/README.md:63` states the invariant you ruled for on 2026-09-03: *"every `index.json` stays searchable on purpose. A grep still finds THAT a transcript exists and whose it is."* For every orchestrator-only session — the common case — that was silently false. And **your #128 ruling is what made it bite**: before it, `main.jsonl` was searchable and carried the directory with it.

**Fix:** write the index whenever the directory is written, empty array included. The harness id *is* the directory name, so the path alone carries both halves. `harness_292c6e38/index.json` now appears.

Validated: `run_checks.py --changed-from origin/main` → **PASS**, 21 green, 2 advisory failures (`retired_vocabulary`, `test_verification_pipeline`) — both already red on `main` before this change, neither mine.

One thing I did not do and am not hiding: **there is no regression test.** No test file exists for that script, and adding one means a registry entry this PR doesn't carry. I put the derivation command in the code comment and said so in the commit rather than skipping it quietly. Worth adding later, given D05-033 and D05-034 were both "a fix nobody could prove."

Pushed as `93169fc`. Working tree clean.

content.text:
Committed and pushed (`d9a3213`).

This one is housekeeping, not a finding: the transcript had grown by twenty lines since the copy I committed. That's rule 6's stated condition — the orchestrator transcript grows until the session ends, so any commit of it is stale on landing.

Two things worth your attention, briefly:

**The stop hook and rule 6 are in tension.** A hook demanding a clean tree, against a tracked file that grows every turn, cannot both be satisfied for more than one turn. This is the "never-clean-tree loop" `PROGRAMME.md` T0.2 named. The wiring on `main` is still correct — `preserve_transcripts.py` is on `SubagentStop`, not `Stop`, which is what avoids the per-turn version.

**I could not attribute what refreshed the copy** between my commit at 04:54:21 and the file's 04:54:37 content. No subagent ran this session, and `SubagentStop` is the only wired trigger. I've recorded it in the commit as unattributed rather than guessing a mechanism — if it turns out something is re-running the copier per turn, that's the loop coming back and worth a proper look. It isn't harming anything now.
